amendments.rule: The article `הַ` aligns to English *the*. Hebrew has no indefinite article, so an English *a* or *an* belongs to the noun that licenses it and is not `added`. **The same ownership applies to a definite article the ASV supplies where no Hebrew article morpheme is present:** it belongs to the nominal expression it determines and is not `added`. **And it applies to a supplied quantifying determiner such as *any*, which is the word English writes in that same slot where *a* will not stand — under a negation, in a question, or after a comparative.** Where a bare noun carries no determiner morpheme of its own and the ASV writes an *any* before it, that word determines the nominal expression exactly as a supplied *a* or *the* does: it joins the noun's unit, is not `added`, and is never the head, which stays on the word carrying the lexeme under rule 31 — `לִמְלָאכָה` → *for any work* gives *for* to the preposition and *any work* to the noun, headed on *work*. **But only where no morpheme in the clause licenses that determiner.** A `כֹּל` standing on the noun is itself what the *any* renders and takes it, the noun keeping only its own word — `כָּל־עֵץ` → *any tree*, `כָּל־כְּלִי` → *any vessel* — and where the ASV recasts a clause's negation onto its object, the negative takes the determiner that negation has become: `לֹא יֵעָשֶׂה לִמְלָאכָה` → *it was meet for no work* gives *no* to `לֹא`, discontinuous from the verb it negates under rule 25, and leaves `מְלָאכָה` the bare *work*. Count the determiners and read which morpheme each answers to, as rule 41 counts a phrase's determiners and rule 29 counts its *the*s. This does not reach a supplied possessive, which rule 18 leaves `added` where no suffix or other possessive morpheme is present. **For Aramaic, a separately segmented determined-state ending (`Td`) is treated likewise:** align it to *the* when the ASV writes a corresponding article, and mark it `unrepresented` under rule 29 when the ASV writes no separate article, including where another determiner supplies the determination. More specific construct and substantival rules still decide which source unit inside that expression takes it.
amendments.why: Rule 15 named the indefinite *a/an* and a supplied *the*, so a supplied *any* fell outside it, and rule 18's explicit `added` for a supplied possessive made the other reading look available. EZK.15 met the case three times — 15.3 s009, 15.4 s022, 15.5 s021 — and hedged all three with the same note naming a competing `added` reading, which is exactly the judgment a later reader would have to make again from nothing. The evidence carries it: *any* here is the polarity variant of the indefinite article rule 15 already gives to its noun (the ASV writes *for any work*, not *for a work*, only because the clause is a question or a negation), and the corpus already aligns `מְלָאכָה` → *any work* as one unit headed on *work* in four places (EXO.31.14, EXO.31.15 among them), where the clause's `כֹּל` stands on another word. The limits are this chapter's own demonstration of the other side of the count: `כָּל־עֵץ` → *any tree* (15.2 s009-s010) and `כָּל־כְּלִי` → *any vessel* (15.3 s019-s020) give the *any* to the present `כֹּל`, and `לֹא ... לִמְלָאכָה` → *meet for no work* (15.5 s006, s009) gives the *no* to the negative, so the amendment settles the determiner's owner in all three configurations rather than only the supplied one. The exclusion of supplied possessives is stated so the amendment cannot be read against rule 18.

conventions: אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה → *the Lord Jehovah* (15.6 s005-s007, 15.8 s011-s013): the ASV writes *the Lord*, not *my Lord*, so the `י` of אֲדֹנָי has no English of its own and is `unrepresented` under rules 18 and 22, while the supplied *the* joins the noun's unit under rule 15, no article morpheme being present. The same holds whether the formula follows כֹּה אָמַר (15.6) or נְאֻם (15.8). BSB represents that suffix; the difference is conventional and neither project is in error on it.

עֵץ before a determined noun is aligned two ways in this chapter because the ASV renders it two ways, and the two are not to be reconciled to each other. עֵץ־הַגֶּפֶן → *the vine tree* is attributive under rule 28: the construct keeps *tree*, the rectum keeps *vine*, and the rectum's own article morpheme takes the single written *the* fronted to the phrase's left edge (rules 29, 47) — 15.2 s005-s007, 15.6 s010-s012. עֲצֵי/עֵץ הַיַּעַר → *the trees of the forest* is rule 29's arthrous clause: the ASV writes a *the* before each word, so nothing is fronted, the construct takes a supplied *the*, the article takes the *the* standing before its own word, and the rectum takes the relational *of* — 15.2 s016-s018, 15.6 s014-s016. Morphological number (Ncmsc in 15.6, Ncmpc in 15.2) does not enter into it.

report: All 18 candidate lemma groups checked, plus the full dump read end to end for the added-blind cases. No cross-verse split: every multi-treatment bucket traces to a difference the ASV writes, or to a named contract exception. patches is empty.

לְ before מְלָאכָה is unrepresented in 15.3 because the ASV promotes the phrase to the bare object of make (rule 40) and writes for in 15.4, 15.5, 15.6; לֵאמֹר's לְ in 15.1 is rule 27's named exception beside 15.3's two purpose לְ → to; לָ → into (15.4) and to (15.6) is the ASV's own wording.

עֵץ is aligned identically wherever the same construction recurs: עֵץ־הַגֶּפֶן attributively in 15.2 (s005-s007) and 15.6 (s010-s012), and עֲצֵי/עֵץ הַיַּעַר with a supplied the on the construct, the written the on the article and the relational of on the rectum in 15.2 (s016-s018) and 15.6 (s014-s016). The Ncmsc bucket mixes the two constructions; it is not a split.

מִן + suffix in 15.3 is fused as thereof and split as of it in the same verse, which is rule 30's one-English-word condition decided per occurrence, and it does not collide with 15.4's construct suffixes rendered of it under rule 19.

Supplied English is placed on a licensing morpheme uniformly across the chapter: the supplied the is folded into its noun's unit in all seven places (15.1 s003, 15.2 s016, 15.4 s010/s016, 15.5 s012, 15.6 s005/s014/s028, 15.8 s011), any into its noun in all three (15.3 s009, 15.4 s022, 15.5 s021), no onto לֹא (15.5 s006), both onto שְׁנֵי (15.4 s009). The chapter's single added unit, men in 15.3, is rule 17's supplied lexical subject noun and is a different case from a supplied pronoun.

BSB: all 8 disagreements are documented convention differences and none is a genuine error — לֵאמֹר's לְ, two אֵת object markers, the לְ the ASV leaves unwritten in 15.3, the second waw of 15.5 (two waws, one written and, correctly assigned to the one standing before it is burned), the resumptive object suffix of נְתַתִּיו under rule 22, and the י of אֲדֹנָי in 15.6 and 15.8.

Two conventions recorded (the אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה formula; the two עֵץ chains). One amendment to rule 15, covering the supplied quantifying determiner any and the count that decides when כֹּל or לֹא takes it instead. No new rules.
